fields.meta_title: Relationship Quiz: How Do You Two Connect? | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Play an eight-question relationship quiz that names how you and your partner connect, or build one for couples that scores every match.
fields.h1: Build a Relationship Quiz That Shows How You Two Connect
fields.hero_description: Build a relationship quiz that scores couples or names a connection style, or play the eight-question quiz below.
fields.features_heading: Inside the Relationship Quiz Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Describe the quiz in one prompt, and Emergent builds the questions and results along with a table that stores every answer. Change any of it by asking.
fields.feature_1:
Partners answer about each other

Each partner answers every question twice: once for themselves and once as a guess about the other. The app counts a match whenever a guess lands on the partner's own answer, so a couple sees one score out of 12.
fields.feature_2:
A connection style as the result

Switch to a matching quiz, where every option points to a style such as Conversation First or Easy Routines. The result screen names the style the answers lean toward and explains it in two short lines.
fields.feature_3:
Answers saved without names

Leave the name field out for a class or a workshop, and the app stores each set of answers on its own. The facilitator sees how many people landed on each result and never who chose what.
fields.feature_4:
Each finished quiz is a row

Every completed quiz lands in a database you own, with each pick and the result next to it. Sort by result before a session, or filter for the couples who scored under 8.
fields.feature_5:
Built for a phone on the couch

Couples tap through one question per screen with a progress bar, which suits a link opened on two phones side by side. Emergent sets no cap on how many people can take the quiz.
fields.feature_6:
An alert when someone finishes

Ask for an email or Slack message each time a visitor completes the quiz, with their result in the first line. Publish it on a custom domain, which is included with Emergent and uses credits.

plan.angle: The top 10 is relationship-health and know-your-partner quizzes from counseling sites, nonprofits and magazines, plus a video. A visitor plays an eight-question quiz on this page that names how two partners connect, then sees four real builds: a couples game night scored as matches, a community center workshop that tallies results with no names, a relationship coach whose result page sends a lead alert, and a singles mixer that pairs guests by result. The FAQ covers compatibility, couples games, readiness, careful wording and where answers go.
tab_stories: Priya Raman and Tomas Novak host a game night for 4 couples, each partner answers 12 questions about the other, and the board puts Leah and Sam Okafor first with 11 of 12 matches and June and Ravi Shah last with 6.

Riverside Community Center sends the relationship quiz to the 18 couples in its 6-week premarriage workshop before week 1, answers are saved with no names, and the tally of 36 partners shows Conversation First 14, Shared Projects 9, Easy Routines 8 and New Experiences 5, so facilitator Dana Mercer spends week 1 on talking things through.
Elena Ruiz takes the relationship quiz on coach Andre Whitfield's site, her answers lean Easy Routines, she asks for a 20-minute intro call, and Andre gets an email with her result.

Kim Laurent runs a monthly singles mixer, 40 guests take the relationship compatibility quiz on arrival, and the app pairs guests with the same result into 20 pairs for the first round of conversation.
